_what: How build-reports/person-index.json is rebuilt WITHOUT losing the work of scripts that patch it after the claims build. Read by src/build_person_index.py (which runs the chain) and src/gate_person_index.py (which refuses a rebuild if any writer is missing from here).
_why: On 2026-09-06 a rebuild silently discarded 60 CFL 1945 seasons, 476 club-key rewrites, 2,576 coaching seasons and 1,052 officiating records, because five scripts wrote the index directly and nothing recorded that they must be re-run. It was caught only because one session measured season-holders before and after by hand.

chain.adds: club-key normalisation from build/club-key-normalisation.json; marks each rewritten season with _club_as_printed
chain.must_precede: apply_person_merges.py -- its own docstring: the index must be normalised BEFORE merging, because merges union seasons by key

chain.adds: build/person-merges.json, RE-applied: the builder applies merges at build time, but club-key normalisation runs after that and may change keys, so merges are applied again (undo-then-apply, idempotent)
chain.must_precede: apply_promotions.py -- the promotion decisions were made against the MERGED index (promote_coaches.py: 'checked_against ... AFTER the 92 merges'); applying them before merges could attach a season to an absorbed record

chain.adds: coaching_seasons, entered_by, promotion_ref, _playing_fields_do_not_apply from build/coach-promotions.json; creates the coaching-only people
reverses the 201 promoted coaches with no coaching stint (build/coach-demotions.json)
the 60 CFL 1945 season keys the ingest never wrote as stints (build/cfl1945-season-restore.json)
chain.runs_last_because: it writes final-form keys CFL|1945|CFLCGY and CFL|1945|CFLWPG and skips a key already present; club-key-normalisation.json does rewrite CFLCGY/CFLWPG codes (though no 1945 entry today), so running AFTER normalisation guarantees the restored keys are never un-normalised or duplicated

chain.adds: the 978 officials created by ingest_officials.py (name, roles, officiating_seasons, identified_by.officials_pfa_code) plus officiating_seasons on the 74 players who already existed -- 1,052 men from build/pfa-officials.json
chain.runs_last_because: MEASURED, not assumed: today it has no hard dependency on any earlier step -- 0 official ids are absorbed by a person-merge, 0 collide with a promoted coach id, 0 share a person_id or a PFA code with the 201 demoted coaches, and officials carry no playing seasons for apply_club_keys to rewrite. It is placed last because that is the position that stays correct if any of those becomes non-zero: running after the merges attaches officiating to the surviving record rather than an absorbed one, and running after demote_stintless re-establishes as an OFFICIAL any man that step removes as a coach, which is what Ryan's ruling requires.
chain.idempotent: YES, in both directions. Every value is a pure function of build/pfa-officials.json and is SET rather than skipped, so a fresh index and a half-applied one converge to the same result. Its report is built from all 1,052 men every run rather than from that run's delta -- which is the specific way apply_promotions.py is NOT idempotent: run by hand against an index that already holds its ids it writes an EMPTY coach-seasons-promoted.json over a good one.
chain.own_output_not_covered_by_rollback: build/officials-applied.json. The rollback restores the INDEX only, so after a rollback this report describes a run that was undone. Re-running the script fixes it.

_order_note: Steps 1->2, 2->3 and 3->4 are hard dependencies (see must_precede). Step 5's position is a safety rule, not a hard dependency today: with the current normalisation file either position gives the same index. Keep it last anyway.

exempt.index_io.py: the atomic-write helper itself; every writer above goes through save_index

how_a_new_patcher_is_picked_up: It is not picked up automatically -- it FAILS LOUDLY. gate_person_index.py scans every src/*.py for a write to the index (open(<index>,'w'), save_index(, dump_atomic(...,<index>)). Any writer not named in `chain` or `exempt` fails P1 by filename with the offending line, and build_person_index.py refuses to rebuild while P1 fails. To add a patcher: write it using index_io.save_index, then add it to `chain` in the right position with `must_precede` / `adds` filled in.
_known_missing_steps_note: Emptied 2026-09-06: the officials applier that was recorded here is now src/apply_officials.py, step 6 of the chain.

held_stores._what: stores the builder reads, COUNTS and REPORTS but does not index, pending a ruling. Not a silent skip: build_person_index prints them and writes them to build-reports/person-index-skipped.json on every build.

store_league_tokens._what: build_person_index derives a stint's league from the STORE FILENAME (stats-nfl-1987 -> NFL). A store whose name is not its league is declared here.
store_league_tokens.assistants: COACHES -- the media guides' staff lists are coaching seasons, and they must land on the same key shape as the Coaching Tree's so a guide's role string attaches to the season it corroborates rather than opening a parallel ASSISTANTS league. Declared 2026-09-07 with Ryan's ruling that a club's own guide naming a man as its coach documents that he worked that season.

identity_is_edited_in_place: unify_identity.py assigns global ids by ENUMERATION ORDER, so re-running it against a changed store set renumbers every person in the archive. build-reports/identity.json is the authority and is edited in place by appliers (src/apply_assistants_identity.py), exactly as the person merges are. Do not re-run unify_identity.py --write.

report_stores_not_claim_sources._what: Files under build/ that a CHAIN STEP writes as its own report and that carry a 'claims' key. build_person_index globs build/*.json and reads anything with claims, so without this the index reads its own previous run's output back in as a source.
report_stores_not_claim_sources._why: coach-seasons-promoted.json is apply_promotions' report of what it applied, keyed on the person ids of THAT run. The builder read it as a claim store and minted 1,598 empty people (no name, no seasons, one pfa.coaching_season each) for the ids of the PREVIOUS generation of promotions. When apply_promotions refreshed the report with the current ids, the next rebuild lost all 1,598 and P3 refused it -- correctly. The index's population must not depend on its own last run. Found 2026-09-07.
report_stores_not_claim_sources.coach-seasons-promoted.json: apply_promotions.py's report. Its claims are a restatement of build/coach-promotions.json, which apply_promotions already applies directly.
report_stores_not_claim_sources._derived_not_only_declared: build_person_index derives this set from the chain scripts themselves (which build/ files they write) and REFUSES to build if a chain step writes a store this declaration does not name. The list is the record; the derivation is the check. Raised by Fetching 2026-09-07: declaring four by name closes four instances, not the class.

2026-09-07.why: They exist only because build_person_index read a chain step's own report (build/coach-seasons-promoted.json, apply_promotions' output) back in as a claim source. They are the person ids of the PREVIOUS generation of promotions: no name, no seasons, no counted field, one pfa.coaching_season person claim each -- a restatement of build/coach-promotions.json, which apply_promotions applies directly to the 1,794 people that carry those seasons now.
